hypothesis: Cali-Tree v2's headline numbers (82.83% full-coverage, 92.87% selective @ 64.25% coverage) come from independent-judge consensus + calibrated abstention / editor-reliability priors, not from the prompt hierarchy (leaves, embeddings, clustering, merge synthesis, routing). If a FLAT single-global-prompt path with the exact same consensus/editor-prior/selective-policy fitting reproduces those numbers, the tree contributes nothing beyond that machinery.

implementation.change: Added architecture={hierarchical,rubric_lite} to the calitree_train node executor (vejudge/interface/node_calibration/calitree_nodes.py). architecture=rubric_lite skips embedding, leaf specialization, semantic clustering, and merge synthesis entirely: the tree starts and ends as one global node. It then runs the identical three-way consensus resolver (_consensus_result), editor-reliability-prior fitting (_fit_editor_prior), and selective-policy fitting (_fit_selective_policy) that the hierarchical path uses -- byte-identical downstream code, zero special-casing.
implementation.critical_fix: The first attempt skipped CaliTreeBuilder.build() entirely, which is also where the hierarchical path's 'textgrad' warm-start candidate is produced. Without it, tree.get('warm_start_prompt') fell back to initial_prompt, so the 'initial' and 'textgrad' consensus candidates were the literal same prompt -- the three-way consensus degenerated to 'trust the base rubric unless critic ties', not a real test. Fixed by running a genuine global TextGrad optimization pass (RubricLiteLearner, the same optimizer Rubric-Lite's own training node uses) to produce tree['warm_start_prompt'] before judging. Verified the fix took effect: warm_start_prompt != initial_prompt post-fix, and partial F1 recovered from 0.0 (broken) to a real (non-degenerate) value.

dev_120_broken.note: First attempt, missing warm-start candidate (see critical_fix). Kept for the record, not used for the confirmation.

full_1200_confirmation.note: Checkpoint-resumed from the dev-120-fixed run; all 232 train-side calls (including the warm-start optimization) were reused, only the additional 1,200-test-case judge/critic/consensus calls were newly billed (~4,763 total judge calls end to end).

conclusion: CONFIRMED: a flat single-global-prompt judge with no embeddings, no leaves, no clustering, no merges, and no routing -- running only three-way consensus, an editor-reliability prior, and a fitted selective-abstention policy -- reproduces frozen Cali-Tree v2's full-1,200-case numbers within 0.1-3pp on every full-coverage metric, and MATCHES OR SLIGHTLY EXCEEDS v2's deployable selective headline (93.14% accepted accuracy @ 63.17% coverage, n=758, versus v2's 92.87% @ 64.25%, n=771). The only metric where the flat path meaningfully trails is partial recall/F1 (-3.0pp / -2.9pp), consistent with this session's other finding that partial is a signal problem independent of architecture. This closes the 'first confirming experiment' from docs/calitree_status.md: the prompt hierarchy (leaves, embeddings, semantic clustering, merge synthesis, routing) is not the source of Cali-Tree v2's accuracy or its selective-abstention win. Both are fully attributable to independent-judge consensus plus calibrated editor-reliability priors, which are architecture-agnostic and now demonstrated to work without any tree underneath them.
caveats: Single run, no repeats/bootstrap CI on the flat path itself (frozen v2's 82.83% carries a bootstrap CI of 80.67-84.92% per docs/calitree.md; the flat path's 82.75% falls comfortably inside that interval, but its own CI was not separately computed).

The flat path's warm-start optimization ran once (3 max steps, same budget as v2's global warm start) on the identical 176-case fit split; a different optimizer seed/budget could shift the specific prompt found.

Editor-reliability prior and selective-policy fitting are identical code paths shared with v2 by construction -- this experiment isolates the hierarchy specifically, not the calibration machinery, which was never in question.
